old_caption:

The scene is dominated by sleek, contemporary buildings with reflective glass facades, which stand tall against a backdrop of a clear blue sky dotted with fluffy white clouds. The sun shines brightly from the right side of the frame, casting a warm glow over the entire scene and creating lens flares that add a dynamic visual element.

caption:
A moving view passes over an elevated bridge path. Its reddish-brown deck, split by a dark central seam and bordered by grey metal railings, narrows toward the city skyline. Dense green trees line the left side, while modern office blocks rise ahead: reflective glass cubes, dark-brick towers, and bright facades catching the sun. A strong lens flare glows in the upper right beneath scattered clouds in a blue sky.

As the view shifts, the bridge deck and railings slide toward the right. The left foliage remains thick, and the street and slender lamp post beside the left railing become more visible. The central glass cube and surrounding towers stay roughly fixed in the distance, with the sun flare holding its place in the upper right.

No people or vehicles occupy the path itself. The bright sun continues to wash the glass facades with warm, hazy light, and the bridge path drifts steadily across the scene, keeping the city skyline centered.

This is a TEMPORALLY CROPPED EXCERPT from a longer video, not a complete event or a loop.
The first view may already be mid-action; the last view need not contain completion. Different
endpoints are normal, not physical errors. Do not add unseen causes, onset, stopping or outcomes.
An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless
the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.
Compare several frames before asserting translation, rotation, direction, unchanged position or
camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

Retain the WISA English narrative style, detail density and paragraph structure. Aim for the
provided original word count within 85%-115%, using genuinely visible details and process.
Do not add repetition, watermark/logo descriptions or atmospheric filler to reach a word count.
Do not shorten a rich caption into a terse technical checklist. Avoid annotation phrases such as
'this mid-segment', 'the excerpt', 'the frame', 'these images', 'observed evidence' in the caption.
This is a direct video description, not an analysis note. No mandatory beginning/end formula.
Complete every sentence. If accuracy requires a substantial length difference, explain it outside
the caption; do not fill missing context by imagination. Optional synonym edits are not needed.

"problem":"concrete visual mismatch or unsupported assertion"}], "caption":"complete final caption",
"length_note":"empty unless required"}. Keep means unchanged caption and no issues. An edit
must actually correct the cited issue. This is a fallible automatic review, not proof of correctness.

draft_caption:
A continuous forward-tracking view steadily moves along an elevated pedestrian bridge path. Its reddish-brown deck narrows toward the horizon, bordered by grey metal railings, while lush green trees crowd the left side. Ahead, a cluster of modern office buildings rises under a bright sun, reflective glass cubes and dark-brick towers catching light, while a prominent lens flare glows in the upper right and scattered clouds drift across a blue sky above the city.

As the viewpoint advances, the deck and railings grow larger and slide toward the frame edges. The left-side foliage thickens near the camera, while the road and grassy verge below the right railing become more prominent. The distant buildings and sun flare remain roughly centered, shifting only slightly, so the scene reads as steady forward movement along the bridge, not a turn.

No people or vehicles occupy the walkway itself, keeping the perspective clean. A slender lamp post beside the left railing stays visible, and the bright sun continues to wash the glass facades with warm, hazy light, casting soft shadows.
